chapter: The Story — A Maze, Four Characters, Moving Cheese
idea: Life's 'cheese' moves: jobs, skills, and situations change constantly — the question is whether you run with the change or stay sniffing an empty station.
application: When weekly reviews show a strategy stopped working (streaks collapsed, focus gone), treat it as moved cheese — re-adapt the plan, not the excuse.

chapter: The Characters — Sniff, Scurry, Hem, Haw
idea: Sniff sniffs change early, Scurry acts immediately, Hem resists and denies, Haw learns to laugh and adapt — everyone is all four, at different times.
application: Name which character your planning style is acting like today; propose tasks that grow the Sniff (scan for signals) and Scurry (act small, now).

idea: Change happens — they keep moving the cheese. Anticipate it, get ready, monitor the supply, and leave before it runs out.
application: Build drift-detection into weekly reviews: if a pattern's numbers keep declining for two weeks in a row, act on it (rather than watch).

idea: Adapt to change quickly; the quicker you let go of old cheese, the sooner you enjoy new cheese.
application: Archived or done work should stay archived — do not resurrect dead approaches; instead, propose the fresh next experiment.

idea: Savor the adventure and move with the cheese: enjoying the journey through the maze makes adaptation itself rewarding.
application: Frame new-skill tasks (new stack, new domain) as adventures with visible progress markers so momentum survives the discomfort.

idea: Be ready to change quickly and enjoy it again — the maze keeps moving even after you adapt once.
application: Keep weekly reviews forward-looking: past wins are hedged by preparing the next change, not by repetition of the same routine forever.

chapter: Haw learns to laugh at himself — Wall Thought
idea: When Haw could finally laugh at himself, he changed — imagining his own fears made the maze scarier than it was.
application: When the user hesitates on a task due to perfectionism or scary imagination, shrink the next step until 'start' takes ten minutes.

chapter: Tim's takeaway — Taking Yourself Too Seriously
idea: Bureaucratic defense of 'my cheese' (my process, my way) is often self-image protection; loosening grip unlocks change.
application: When tasks center on protecting a familiar process rather than progress, ask if the model needs updating instead of defending it.
